#6226. Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card Review: Strong Bonus Categories, Weak Overall Value

Both American Express and Chase issue co-branded Marriott credit cards, meaning consumers have lots of options to choose from. This is my Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card review, as I’d like to take a look at whether this Marriott credit card is worth it.

Personally I don’t think that the Bonvoy Bevy Card is Marriott’s most compelling credit card option, and given how the offers on some cards are mutually exclusive, I think there’s a better strategy. However, everyone should decide for themselves, based on their own situation. Let’s look at the value proposition of the Bonvoy Bevy Card, including the welcome offer, annual fee, return on spending, and perks, so you can make your own decision.

Link: Learn more about the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card

Before I get into the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card review, let me give you a high-level summary of the card’s main features and perks:

I also put together my list of the top pros and cons for the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card:

When applying for a credit card, obviously the welcome bonus, eligibility rules, and fees, are major factors that people consider. After all, this determines how much value you can get upfront, and also how much this card will cost you in the long run. With that in mind, let’s take at the bonus and fee details for the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card.

The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card currently has a welcome offer where you can earn 85,000 Bonvoy bonus points after spending $5,000 within the first six months. Based on my latest miles & points valuations, Bonvoy points are worth 0.7 cents each, meaning I value the welcome offer at $595.

This is the standard welcome offer on the card, though we’ve definitely seen better bonuses in the past. For example, in the past I recall seeing a bonus of up to 125,000 points plus a $150 statement credit upon completing minimum spending. So it could be worth waiting to apply to see if a higher offer comes back around.

If applying for the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card, Amex’s general application restrictions apply, and on top of that, there are some additional restrictions for Marriott credit card eligibility.

The most important thing to understand is that you are eligible for this card, including the welcome offer, if you have the Marriott Bonvoy Business® American Express® Card (learn more). However, you aren’t eligible for the welcome offer if you have the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card (learn more).

The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card has a $250 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and you can add authorized users at no extra cost.

Among Marriott personal credit cards, this card has the second-highest annual fee (there are also no annual fee and $95 annual fee options), with the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card (learn more) being the only card with a higher annual fee — it has a $650 annual fee (Rates & Fees).

The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card is supposed to be the best credit card for actually earning points, so the card has a pretty decent rewards structure. The card offers the following return on spending, all with no foreign transaction fees:

Ultimately these are just about the best bonus categories you’ll see on a co-branded Marriott credit card. However:

The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card offers a variety of perks for being a cardmember. Some perks are offered just for having the card, while other perks require spending or other activity. Let’s go over the details, in no particular order.

The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card offers 1,000 bonus points per paid eligible stay with Marriott, which is a perk that’s unique to this card. You need to pay for your stay with the card to be eligible, and only paid stays booked directly with Marriott qualify (so third party bookings and award stays don’t count). Bonus points will post within six weeks of an eligible stay.

For the very frequent Marriott guest, this has the potential to be pretty useful, especially if you make frequent, short stays. Based on my valuation of Bonvoy points, this is like an incremental return of roughly $7 per paid stay.

Unfortunately, the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card doesn’t offer a free night award just for being a cardmember. Rather, you can earn a free night award valid at a property costing up to 50,000 points when you spend $15,000 on the card in a calendar year.

It’s also possible to top off Marriott free night awards with up to 25,000 additional points to redeem at more expensive properties. This means you could redeem a free night award plus 25,000 points to stay at a hotel costing 75,000 points per night.

This is a disappointing aspect of the card, as several other Marriott credit cards don’t require you to spend any amount to earn such a certificate.

The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card offers complimentary Marriott Bonvoy® Gold Elite status for as long as you’re a cardmember. This is better than nothing, but don’t get too excited. Marriott Gold status offers perks like:

Just for having the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card you receive 15 elite nights toward status annually. This can help you if you’re looking to earn a higher elite tier, like Marriott Bonvoy® Platinum Elite status, Titanium Elite status or Ambassador Elite status, and it can also help you with earning Choice Benefits (like Nightly Upgrade Awards).

It’s also worth noting that you can stack the 15 elite night credits on this card with elite night credits earned on a Marriott business credit card. That gets you a long way toward the Marriott Bonvoy Platinum Elite status requirement of 50 nights.

The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card offers some extra protections both when you’re traveling and making purchases with your card. These include:

Up to $300 per Covered Trip that is delayed for more than 12 hours; and 2 claims per Eligible Card per 12 consecutive month period. Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by New Hampshire Insurance Company, an AIG Company. Baggage insurance plan: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. Car rental loss and damage insurance: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. Car Rental Loss or Damage Coverage is offered through American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. Extended warranty and purchase protection: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company.

Looking at the card in isolation, there’s a case to be made for getting the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card, especially if you’re a very frequent Marriott guest. If you put all your Marriott spending on the card, you’d earn 1,000 bonus points per stay, 6x points on Marriott spending, and you could earn a free night award after spending $15,000.

But even if you’re set on a Marriott credit card, there are better options, as I view it, especially given how some cards are (somewhat) mutually exclusive, at least when it comes to welcome offers.

If you ask me, the Bonvoy Bevy Card is the weakest card in the Marriott credit card portfolio in terms of value for the annual fee, and I think you’re much better off going for the higher annual fee card.

The Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant Card (learn more) has a $650 annual fee, and offers:

As I see it, the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant Card’s annual fee easily pays for itself, between the dining credit, anniversary free night award, elite status, Priority Pass™ membership, and more.

The Marriott Bonvoy Boundless® Credit Card (learn more) has a lower annual fee of $95, but in my opinion it offers significantly more value than the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card. Its perks include:

The free night award alone makes this card worth it. You get this once every account anniversary year, and you can top off the free night with an additional 25,000 points. Even though the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card’s free night award is valid for rooms that cost up to 50,000 points, it’s not worth spending $15,000 on the card in a year just to earn it.

If you’re not actually that committed to the Marriott Bonvoy ecosystem, there are lots of other great cards to consider. In particular, these are cards with relatively reasonable annual fees and great rewards structures, and they’re very well rounded:

The Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card has a $250 annual fee, and offers some solid bonus categories, plus 1,000 Bonvoy bonus points per stay. The card also offers Bonvoy Gold Elite status, 15 elite nights annually for being a cardmember, and a free night award when you spend $15,000 on the card in a calendar year.

Ultimately, I’d say this is a pretty weak card, especially compared to the rest of Marriott’s card portfolio. It doesn’t offer statement credits or an automatic free night award to offset the annual fee, and you can’t even spend your way to a higher status level on this card. Personally, I’d much rather get the Marriott Bonvoy Boundless Card or Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant Card, as I think the cards represent a better overall value.

What do you make of the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy Card?

I just combined three Target deals to earn $30 in Target gift cards and rewards on $200 in Disney e-gift cards I needed anyway. And I did it all from my couch in just a few minutes.

And if you are sad this doesn't include Target gift cards, I'd stay tuned, as in the last few years Target has offered a one- or two-day sale of 10% off Target gift cards for Target Circle members, so it is certainly possible that will return, too.

#6224. Air Algerie VIP Lounge Algiers Airport Review: Strong Furniture Store Vibes

For the next stop of my Orient Express adventure via Africa trip, I had the chance to visit the Air Algerie VIP Lounge at Algiers Houari Boumediene International Airport (ALG). I had just landed from Montreal (YUL) in Air Algerie’s A330neo business class, and was connecting to Tunis (TUN) in Air Algerie’s A320 business class (a wet leased flight).

The Air Algerie VIP Lounge Algiers is actually pleasant enough. It’s quirky, as it has a ton of seating, and almost feels more like a furniture store than an airport lounge. But I appreciate that the space isn’t crowded, so it’s a nice enough place to pass some time. The food and drink selection is totally unremarkable and okay, so at least it’s not negatively memorable.

The Algiers Airport transit experience was interesting. Algeria is a country that really doesn’t want tourists (getting a visa is a pain), and Air Algerie doesn’t get much connecting international traffic, so not that many people are in international transit.

Upon landing from Montreal, I followed the signage in the direction of “Flight Connections.” Interestingly, I seemed to be among the only people on my flight with an international connection, as everyone else headed to immigration.

I ended up in the “transit room,” as it’s called. There my boarding pass was checked, and then I was given a form that I had to fill out. A form to transit internationally? Odd, but whatever. I then had to wait for an immigration officer to be ready, but he just seemed to be sitting in his window for several minutes without signaling he was ready, so I just waited.

After about five minutes, it was my turn. Then there was a security check, except the security guy clearly wasn’t quite ready yet for anyone, so he was caught off guard by me, and took a second to set things up.

All-in-all, it was a painless enough transit experience thanks to the lack of crowds, even if it was a bit bureaucratic. The Algiers Airport terminal is really big, and it just felt totally deserted during my early morning visit (when a lot of flights leave, in theory).

Once in the international departures area, it was easy to find the Air Algerie VIP Lounge, as there was signage for it right there. The lounge is in the center of the terminal, up a level, so you can either take the elevator, escalator, or stairs.

Once on the upper level, the entrance to the lounge was right there. I loved the Air Algerie Boeing 767 airplane model at the entrance. I’m not sure if this was intended to be a throwback, or if they just hadn’t bothered getting a new model in the nearly decade since the aircraft type was retired. I have a guess, but… 😉

The Air Algiers VIP Lounge Algiers is open 24/7, or something like that. The hours aren’t actually published, but the idea is that if there are flights, then the lounge should also be open.

The Air Algerie VIP Lounge is the primary lounge at Algiers Airport. So in addition to being open to premium passengers on Air Algerie, it also acts as the contract lounge for premium passengers on EgyptAir, Qatar Airways, Royal Jordanian, Saudia, Tunisair, and Turkish Airlines.

Oddly, the lounge isn’t open to Priority Pass members, despite clearly having the capacity to handle more passengers.

The Air Algerie VIP Lounge Algiers is quite a large facility, especially in relation to demand. The lounge basically consists of one large room, and it “opens up” into the rest of the terminal, as it’s essentially just on top of the main passenger concourse.

As I said above, the only way I can describe this lounge is as having very strong furniture store vibes, as there’s just a sea of couches and chairs, all of which are quite plush. I’ll let the pictures speak mostly for themselves.

The lounge was really quiet during my visit. There were maybe a total of a dozen people in the lounge, and I’d say fewer than half of those were passengers, and the remainder were airport staff having their morning coffee, and helping themselves to the buffet.

The lounge was quite well staffed — there were two staff members responsible for overseeing the buffet, while for reasons I can’t figure out, there were three people at the front desk of the lounge (I don’t think a single other person entered during my hour stay, so that strikes me as an overkill, but…).

The Air Algerie VIP Lounge Algiers has a self-serve food & drink selection.

When it comes to food, the selection included finger sandwiches, whole fruit, veggies, cheese, cold cuts, yogurt, cereal, pastries, etc.

There were also some hot options, none of which looked particularly appealing to me (and I also wondered for how long these items had been sitting around). This included eggs, sausage, potatoes, and veggies.

When it comes to drinks, this is a “dry” lounge (so there’s no alcohol). Options included coffee, tea, soft drinks, and water, all of which guests could help themselves to.

The Air Algerie VIP Lounge Algiers has bathrooms that are located just inside the entrance and to the right. They’re down a hall, right next to the kitchen area.

The men’s room had three sinks, three toilet stalls, and two urinals.

In theory there was also a shower suite, but as you can see below, not really.

The Air Algerie VIP Lounge Algiers was the best part of my Air Algerie experience, which isn’t saying a whole lot. The carrier’s flagship lounge is large, and has an okay selection of food and drinks. In an era where so many lounges are crowded, it’s at least nice to have a quiet space like this.

Admittedly this is otherwise a pretty uninteresting lounge, with few amenities, and a lack of variety when it comes to seating options. I definitely wouldn’t arrive early to use this lounge, but it’s also not a bad place to pass some time.

What do you make of the Air Algerie VIP Lounge Algiers?

#6223. Lufthansa Suddenly Cancels This 13-Hour Nonstop Route: See Map Now

Last month, Lufthansa announced its most extensive route expansion since 2020. For summer 2027, the Star Alliance member is adding ten new long-haul routes across Asia and the Americas, as well as increasing frequencies on several existing services.

While not part of the announcement, the German flag carrier was also scheduled to resume nonstop flights between Munich Airport (MUC) and Hong Kong International Airport (HKG) after several years of absence. However, in its latest weekend schedule update, the airline removed the route altogether.

Lufthansa has been connecting Germany and Hong Kong since 1961, initially operating flights from Frankfurt Airport (FRA). In the 2000s, the airline also introduced flights from Munich. The route continued operating until early 2020 and has remained suspended since then. The German flag carrier was scheduled to resume flights between Munich and Hong Kong on March 28, 2027, using the Airbus A350-900.

This was also the aircraft type used on the route before its suspension in 2020. In fact, over the years, the airline has operated multiple widebody aircraft on the route, including the Airbus A340-300 and A340-600. It also deployed its Airbus A380 superjumbo in 2018 and 2019.

Why Lufthansa has decided not to reinstate the Munich–Hong Kong route remains unknown. Nevertheless, Cathay Pacific, which is Hong Kong's largest airline, will continue to connect the two cities. The airline launched four weekly flights between Munich and Hong Kong in June last year, operating on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, using its A350-900 aircraft.

Lufthansa, meanwhile, will continue to serve Hong Kong from its Frankfurt hub, using the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner. According to schedule data from aviation analytics provider Cirium, the airline is scheduled to operate one daily round-trip flight on the route throughout the year. Cathay Pacific also offers daily flights between Frankfurt and Hong Kong.

This means there will be a total of 18 weekly services from Germany to Hong Kong next summer. Looking more broadly, the German airline is scheduled to operate 76 weekly flights across 11 East Asian routes in summer 2027. These include the return of services to Nagoya and Tokyo Narita in Japan, both from its Frankfurt hub.

From March 29, 2027, the Star Alliance member will operate three weekly flights to Chubu Centrair International Airport (NGO), which it last served in 2020. A day earlier, on March 28, it will also resume daily flights to Tokyo Narita Airport (NRT). The airline last operated passenger flights to Narita in 2017, when it consolidated its Tokyo operations at Haneda Airport (HND).

In general, Lufthansa has been expanding its network from both Frankfurt and Munich. The airline introduced several new destinations this winter and has more routes planned for summer 2027. From its Southern hub, it will launch three weekly flights to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) on August 3, operating on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays with the A350-900. It will also increase frequencies to Bangalore, Chicago, São Paulo and Singapore.

It would not be surprising to see the German flag carrier adding more routes from Munich in the future, especially given its plans to expand its long-haul operations at the airport. It has extended its joint venture agreement with Munich Airport until 2056. Under the agreement, both parties plan to expand terminal infrastructure and support the growth of Lufthansa's long-haul fleet and operations at the airport.

Munich is already home to the airline's A380 fleet and remains its main hub for the A350-900. According to Cirium schedule data, the airline has scheduled about 6,341 flights using the A350-900 from Munich between January and October 2027, compared to 1,492 from Frankfurt. This is an increase of 7% at Munich and 70% at Frankfurt compared to the same period in 2026.

#6222. Atmos Rewards Credit Card Bonus Offers & Eligibility Rules Explained

Atmos Rewards is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, and the program has three co-branded credit cards in the United States — the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card, Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card, and Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card — all of which are excellent.

In this post, I’d like to go over the details of the welcome offers on these cards. After that, I’ll talk a bit about card eligibility. Let me say up front that it’s possible to get more than one of these cards, so you’re probably eligible for one of these even if you already have a card in the portfolio.

Link: Learn about the best credit cards for Alaska Atmos Rewards

Bank of America and Alaska Air Group partner on issuing three co-branded credit cards, all with Atmos Rewards branding, replacing the previous Mileage Plan program. Let’s cover the details of the bonuses, plus the basics of why you may want to consider these cards.

The Atmos Rewards Summit Card has a $395 annual fee, and is the most premium personal card in the collection.

The card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you can receive 100,000 bonus points and a 25,000-point Global Companion Award with this offer. To qualify, spend $6,000 or more on purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account.

While this card has the highest annual fee of the three cards, it offers an amazing value proposition. Perks include the following, among other things:

Read a detailed review of the Atmos Rewards Summit Card.

The Atmos Rewards Ascent Card has a $95 annual fee, and is the more basic of the two personal cards in the collection.

The card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you can receive 60,000 bonus points and a $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes and fees from $23) after spending $3,000 or more on purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account. You can earn an additional 20,000 bonus points after spending a total of $5,000 or more on purchases within the same 90-day period.

This is a great option for a low-fee card that still offers considerable value for someone who flies Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency. Some of the card’s perks include the following:

Read a detailed review of the Atmos Rewards Ascent Card.

The Atmos Rewards Business Card has a minimum of a $95 annual fee ($70 for the account and $25 per card), and is the business card in the portfolio.

The card is offering a welcome bonus of 70,000 bonus points and a $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes and fees from $23) after you make $4,000 or more in purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account.

The perks on this card are very similar to the perks on its personal card equivalent. These include the following, among other things:

Read a detailed review of the Atmos Rewards Business Card.

With the above out of the way, who is eligible for the welcome offers on the Atmos Rewards Summit Card, Atmos Rewards Ascent Card, and Atmos Rewards Business Card?

Let me start by stating that eligibility for all three Atmos Rewards cards (including the welcome offers) is considered independently. So if you already have the Atmos Rewards Ascent Card, you can apply for the Atmos Rewards Summit Card, and vice versa. The same is true for the Atmos Rewards Business Card. So rules can’t get easier in that regard.

How does card eligibility work if you have an existing Alaska Airlines Bank of America card, or Hawaiian Airlines Barclays card?

Let’s start with the easier part of the answer. If you have or have had either of the Hawaiian Airlines Barclays cards (whether personal or business) that doesn’t impact your ability to qualify for any of the Atmos Rewards cards, including the welcome bonuses.

Meanwhile if you have any former Alaska Airlines Bank of America cards, those cards have been converted (or are in the process of being converted) into one of these new Atmos Rewards cards:

So you may not be eligible for the bonus on one of those cards if you currently have it. However, you’d likely be eligible for the bonus on whichever card you don’t have.

What about if you’ve had one of the above cards in the past? Bank of America doesn’t generally have a “once in a lifetime” rule. Instead, you typically have to wait 24 months from when you closed a card before you can qualify for the bonus on a card again (though some report earning a bonus sooner than that).

However, that’s not a published rule, and you’ll find that offer terms call this a “one-time promotion” that’s “limited to customers opening a new account.”

Beyond the rules specific to the Atmos Rewards cards, what general things should you be aware of if applying for a Bank of America card? Here are the two most common Bank of America restrictions:

Neither of those rules seem to be totally consistently enforced, and in particular, that latter policy doesn’t seem consistent at all. For example, when I applied for Atmos Rewards cards last year, I had opened more than three new cards in the previous 12 months, and was still approved.

How hard are Bank of America cards to get approved for, in general? Obviously this is only based on anecdotal reports, but in my experience, Bank of America cards are generally quite easy to get approved for, and I also find they typically have quite large credit limits. However, the issuer can also be quirky with denials, especially based on the above two rules.

There’s no published credit score you need to get approved for Atmos Rewards credit cards, as it’s one of only many factors that impacts your approval odds. I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range — ideally I’d have a score of 700+ points, but people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

What’s the best play if you’re considering picking up an Atmos Rewards credit card, between the Atmos Rewards Summit Card, Atmos Rewards Ascent Card, and Atmos Rewards Business Card? Honestly, you can’t go wrong with any combination of cards here. A few thoughts:

For example, I’ve shared my experience getting approved for the Atmos Rewards Summit Card, and also my experience getting approved for the Atmos Rewards Business Card.

There are three Atmos Rewards credit cards, including the premium Atmos Rewards Summit Card, plus the Atmos Rewards Ascent Card and Atmos Rewards Business Card.

These are all worthwhile cards, so if you’re eligible for any of these cards, they’re worth considering. One thing that’s great is that eligibility requirements for these cards aren’t too strict, in the sense that you can qualify for each of these cards, and earn the welcome offers. Hopefully the above is a useful rundown of the rules surrounding getting approved for these cards.

Are there any Atmos Rewards credit card application questions I haven’t covered? If you’ve applied for one of these cards, what was your experience like?

Having elite status with an airline can make a significant difference in your travel experience. Shorter lines, faster service, complimentary upgrades, international lounge access and other benefits can easily make stressful trips more seamless. But these perks don't come without a cost, and United MileagePlus overhauled how members earn status in 2026.

This guide will evaluate United Airlines Premier status and break down the different status tiers, how to earn them and whether their perks are worth the effort for United flyers.

Related: Your guide to United MileagePlus

When you choose to fly United and add your MileagePlus number to your booking, in addition to earning miles, you also earn points toward Premier status. Depending on your status tier, elite perks range from complimentary first-class upgrades on most domestic flights (depending on availability) to earning bonus miles that can be redeemed for future travel.

United currently has two ways for members to climb the Premier status ladder:

PQPs are based on a combination of your spending on flights and on eligible United credit cards.

Starting in 2027, PQPs will become the sole elite status metric. As part of those changes, top-tier Premier 1K status will also become even tougher to earn.

The old metrics are still in place through the end of 2026, so we will cover both options.

Related: Why United's elite status changes are bad news for many flyers

Anyone can create a United MileagePlus account for free online. Once you take off on your elite status expedition, you’ll have four official elite status tiers to work toward:

There’s also an unpublished exclusive tier called Global Services, which can only be achieved by flying 4 million miles or receiving a personal invitation.

Here's an overview of what you'll need to earn each status tier before and after the changes.

One requirement that is not changing: You must take at least four flights operated by United or United Express in a calendar year to qualify for any status tier.

When you reach any elite status tier, it is valid for the remainder of the calendar year, the entirety of the following year, and the first month of the year after. For instance, if you reach status requirements anytime in 2026, you will hold the status through Jan. 31, 2028. So, the sooner you earn elite status, the longer you can enjoy the benefits.

Now, let's dive into how to earn PQPs (and, through the end of 2026, PQFs).

Related: Earn MileagePlus miles with United’s airline, hotel and credit card partners

The classic way to earn PQPs is via your spending on flights. The earning rate depends on which airline operates the flight and whether you book it with cash or miles. PQPs are awarded to the passenger, not the person who buys the ticket.

Earn 1 PQP for every 6 award miles on MileagePlus partner airlines, up to a maximum of 500 PQPs per flight in economy and premium economy and 1,000 PQPs per flight in first and business class.

You can also earn PQPs through spending on United's cobranded credit cards. None of these cards provide complimentary elite status, but you’ll earn PQPs on everyday purchases (up to a certain amount), and some cards offer PQPs as part of the welcome bonus.

The information for the United Club Business Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Although United is making it harder to earn status in 2027, it is also giving existing elite members a boost toward next year's status. If you hold elite status and an eligible United credit card (or open one by Dec. 31, 2026), you will receive 5% of the PQPs required for your current status level at the start of 2027:

Related: The ultimate guide to earning elite status with United cards

The perks of United loyalty get more and more appealing as you climb the Premier status ladder. You'll also earn more MileagePlus miles on United purchases as you gain status, though the number of miles you'll earn also depends on whether you hold a United credit card.

United's lowest elite tier confers benefits such as:

When you reach the Gold tier, you'll receive all the perks of Silver as well as:

At Platinum, you can enjoy all the benefits of Gold, plus:

Members who get all the way to the top are rewarded with the Platinum benefits listed above, in addition to:

On top of the various metrics for earning miles and status, United MileagePlus awards something called PlusPoints, a separate currency available only to Platinum and 1K members.

PlusPoints were originally used for seat upgrades, though these have become harder to get in recent years as demand has skyrocketed. That’s why United introduced several new ways to redeem your PlusPoints, including for bonus miles, PQPs, TravelBank cash and gifting Premier status to other MileagePlus members.

Related: When does airline elite status expire?

Elite status can certainly make travel more comfortable and convenient. If you regularly travel with United or its partner airlines and/or spend significantly on a cobranded credit card, you may find it relatively easy to earn Premier status. And it can be a savvy way to maximize your travel.

Plus, this means you’ll also be earning plenty of United miles, which you can redeem for United award flights — all while enjoying your elite status benefits.

However, it’s not worth pursuing status when you can’t enjoy the benefits you’ve worked hard to earn. Be sure to consider United’s route map, its presence at your home airport and how easy it is to get to your desired destinations. If United and its partner airlines don’t fly where you live or where you want to travel, you won’t get much use from Premier status. You may be better off pursuing status with a different program, such as Delta SkyMiles or American AAdvantage.

Finally, remember that Premier status does not provide domestic lounge access when traveling with United. If this benefit is important to you, consider applying for the , which provides United Club access and perks such as two free checked bags and Premier Access travel services.

Related: Complete guide to United’s fare classes

Earning elite status, especially a top-tier status like Premier 1K, is no easy feat and requires countless hours on planes and thousands of dollars spent. Understanding the cost and perks of United’s elite status is important to determine if it is right for you — especially since United is making status harder to earn in 2027.

Consider your travel plans and whether it makes sense to stay loyal to one airline. If you're interested in earning elite status, check out our guide to airline status matches and challenges and one TPGer's status plans for 2026.

#6220. World of Hyatt Free Night Awards: How To Earn, Redeem, Gift, & Maximize Them

In addition to being able to redeem World of Hyatt points for hotel stays, program members also have the opportunity to earn free night certificates, which can be redeemed for stays at hotels.

In this post, I want to talk about everything you need to know about World of Hyatt free night award certificates — how do you earn them, how can you redeem them, and what are the restrictions associated with them?

There are a variety of ways to earn World of Hyatt award free night certificates:

For some context on the potential value of these certificates:

Note that while World of Hyatt is pretty strict when it comes to the expiration date of free night awards, members can sometimes receive points in exchange for expired certificates. This isn’t a published policy, but rather is an unwritten courtesy that’s sometimes extended to members, so it’s not something you can count on, but it’s worth asking about. This generally only works for awards issued through Milestone Rewards perks, and not those issued through credit cards.

If you want to see your free night award certificates, just log into your World of Hyatt account. Once in there, click on the “Awards” section. There you’ll see how many awards you have, what kind of awards you have, and when they expire (you have to stay by the expiration date, and not just book by then).

You can generally expect that your free night awards will be deposited in your World of Hyatt account within a few weeks of completing eligible activity, though often even faster than that.

The process of redeeming your Hyatt free night awards is pretty easy, and can be done online. There are two ways you can approach this:

As you start to redeem World of Hyatt free night award certificates, there are a few things to note:

With that in mind, I think the easiest way to redeem is to just start searching on hyatt.com. Search availability for the city or hotel you want, and go through the process as if you’re trying to make a points booking, by clicking the “Use Points” button.

You’ll see the hotel results on the next page. You’ll want to select a hotel that shows the points cost as being within the range of the certificate you have (in other words, for a Category 1-4 free night certificate you’d want it to cost no more than 25,000 points per night).

For example, take the Hyatt Regency JFK Airport at Resorts World, which represents a good use of a free night certificate compared to the cash rate.

When you click through and view rates, you’ll be able to select whether you want to redeem your free night award certificate or points.

For what it’s worth, for a random one-night stay on a Friday at this hotel that I pulled up, the cheapest paid rate would be over $500 per night, including taxes and fees.

It’s pretty amazing that a free night certificate offered by the $95 annual fee World of Hyatt Credit Card can be used here.

There are a couple of situations in which you may want to book by phone:

Much like an award night booked using points, stays booked with free night award certificates are eligible for all World of Hyatt elite benefits. If you’re a Globalist member you’ll receive a suite upgrade subject to availability, complimentary breakfast, lounge access, etc. The only restriction is that you can’t redeem a suite upgrade award, club access award, or Guest of Honor award, for stays booked with free night awards (because you can’t stack certificates).

Furthermore, Hyatt stays booked with free night awards are eligible to earn elite qualifying nights, so they can help you jump to the next elite tier, or help you reach the next Milestone Rewards perk.

It’s possible to transfer your World of Hyatt free night awards to others. This is super easy to do. When you’re in the “Awards” section of your World of Hyatt account, just take a look at your free night awards.

To gift an award to another World of Hyatt member, just click the three dots next to the award you want to gift, click the “Gift Your Award” button, and then you’ll be able to transfer your award. You’ll just need the World of Hyatt number and last name of the World of Hyatt member who you’re gifting the award to.

The award will then instantly post to their account, and they can redeem it however they’d like, with the same expiration date.

I figure it makes sense to briefly share my strategy when it comes to redeeming Hyatt free night award certificates. To keep things simple, let me talk about Category 1-4 free night certificates.

While they can be redeemed at properties costing up to 25,000 points per night (in peak season), I wouldn’t value them that high, given the expiration date of the certificates (meanwhile points never expire in conjunction with activity).

Does it only make sense to redeem a Category 1-4 free night certificate at a Category 4 hotel, or under what circumstances could it make sense to redeem at a hotel that requires fewer points? My general approach is as follows:

For example, while I’ve typically used Category 1-4 free night certificates at Category 4 properties, I’ve also a couple of times redeemed them at Category 3 properties, when I wasn’t 100% sure I’d be able to use them otherwise. I think that’s ultimately still a great deal, especially if it’s a property where the cash rate would be high.

Everyone should consider their own situation, though. For example, some people consistently plan all of their travel six or more months in advance, and in that case you wouldn’t want to wait as long as I do to try to maximize certificates.

There are several ways to earn World of Hyatt free night certificates, whether it’s through the World of Hyatt Credit Card, or through the Milestone Rewards program. There’s lots of value to be had with these certificates, and I’ve consistently been able to maximize their value pretty well. Now you can even transfer them to others.

Hopefully the above answers any questions you may have about Hyatt free night award certificates, though if I missed anything, please let me know.

A mother and her 7-year-old son waiting for a flight at the Fort Lauderdale airport were splashed with urine when a man seated across from them exposed himself and began urinating in their direction on Tuesday morning, November 3. Deputies arrested the 48-year old local man on six charges. The arrest affidavit says this happened at gate E6, which tells me this is either an American Airlines or JetBlue passenger. The family said the man was facing them when he unbuttoned his pants and let loose. The father avoided the blast. “Several other passengers were present in the immediate area at the time of the incident,” Powell wrote. “As Raben exposed himself and began urinating, the surrounding passengers dispersed from the area.” The charges were: Battery involving an adult causing a child to come into contact with bodily fluids. Battery. Three counts of indecent exposure. Disorderly intoxication. Go figure: Florida has an actual felony specifically covering an adult knowingly causing, or attempting to cause, a child to come into contact with urine or certain other bodily substances by projecting or expelling them. They knew they needed this. It’s a third-degree felony, punishable by up to five years in prison. He was released on $5,000 bond. Airport surveillance footage of the incident has not been released. Local 10 News reporting on the Fort Lauderdale airport arrest “Urine trouble now, buddy,” one Reddit commenter offered. This happens more than you’d expect (or at least, more than anyone would hope). At Memphis airport a man urinated over a woman sleeping in the terminal. Earlier this year, an Air Canada passenger was filmed urinating on the floor at a Calgary gate while bystanders wondered whether he was sleepwalking. And once you’re on board, getting away becomes harder. A Frontier Airlines passenger who said urine ran onto his leg and shoes was offered a $75 voucher. I’ve been writing about this long enough that the New York Times once interviewed me about what to do when another passenger urinates on you. Nobody should be surprised that the perpetrator in this case was a Florida Man. Though the meme itself is somewhat self-perpetuating, sort of like the 2001 summer of the shark despite no evidence that there was actually any spike in shark attacks. The state’s public records law helps make arrest material accessible, though they’re not alone here. There’s actually academic scholarship arguing it’s our existing priors about Florida that make Florida stories more social shareable. #6218. 3,700 Miles: TAP Air Portugal Unveils New Unusual Longest A321LR Route

TAP Air Portugal is planning a significant change to its Porto–Luanda service, deploying the Airbus A321LR on the 3,737-mile (6,014 km) route from October 31, 2027. The move will create the airline's longest scheduled nonstop A321LR flight, narrowly surpassing its existing Lisbon–Belém service.

The decision is particularly noteworthy because TAP intends to replace its 298-seat Airbus A330-900 with a 171-seat narrowbody, reducing passenger capacity by approximately 43%. The long sector also raises questions about baggage and payload limitations, particularly given the substantial baggage requirements that can characterize routes between Europe and sub-Saharan Africa. The change remains provisional, with almost a year until its planned introduction.

According to AeroRoutes, TAP's preliminary winter 2027/28 schedule replaces the A330-900 with the A321LR on its twice-weekly service from Porto to Luanda. The route connects northern Portugal with Angola's new Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport, which has progressively replaced the city's older airport. The proposed flight schedule is detailed below.

The aircraft substitution will reduce weekly capacity from 1,192 to 684 seats across both directions, a reduction of 508 seats. TAP's A321LR configuration accommodates 16 business-class passengers and 155 economy passengers, compared with 34 business and 264 economy seats on its A330-900s. The smaller aircraft could allow TAP to better match capacity with demand while maintaining nonstop service. When TAP first received the A321LR, then-CEO Antonoaldo Neves explained its strategic importance:

“With its superior range, we can comfortably explore new markets in North America, South America and Africa from Portugal, and offer nonstop flights with the right size of aircraft.”

However, the long flight raises operational questions. Airbus advertises an A321LR range of approximately 4,000 nautical miles, equivalent to 4,603 miles (7,408 km), comfortably exceeding Porto–Luanda's great-circle distance of 3,737 miles (6,014 km) on paper. Nevertheless, the aircraft's range depends on payload and operating conditions.

Heavy checked baggage, commercial cargo, headwinds, and fuel reserves could all influence its performance. TAP has not announced any passenger or baggage restrictions, and whether either will be necessary remains unknown.

The Porto–Luanda deployment will surpass TAP's Lisbon–Belém service by just 11 miles (18 km). The Portuguese flag carrier has increasingly used its A321LRs to connect smaller long-haul markets across the Atlantic, particularly in northeastern Brazil and North America.

Its introduction of the aircraft transformed TAP's transatlantic network, allowing the airline to serve destinations previously impossible to operate economically because they would have required larger widebodies to cover the distance. TAP's planned 2027 A321LR network includes 16 nonstop routes exceeding 2,000 miles (3,219 km).

Six of the ten longest connect Portugal with the Americas, three serve Brazil specifically, and the new Porto–Luanda service is the only African route on the list. The ranking illustrates the versatility of an aircraft that TAP originally introduced to complement its A330-900 fleet. Crucially, the record applies only to nonstop flights: TAP has operated longer one-stop A321LR services, including Lisbon–Belém–Manaus, covering a combined 4,534 miles (7,297 km).

Introduced in November 2024, the three-weekly service was scheduled to take 11 hours and 45 minutes, including its stop in Belém. TAP has also just launched a triangular Lisbon–São Luís–Fortaleza–Lisbon service, demonstrating how intermediate stops extend the reach of its long-haul narrowbody fleet.

Simple Flying had the chance to check out this narrowbody flying over the Atlantic!

The destination is itself undergoing a major transformation. Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport (NBJ) was inaugurated in November 2023, approximately 25 miles (40 km) south-east of central Luanda, replacing Quatro de Fevereiro Airport (LAD) as the city's principal passenger gateway.

Angola's national carrier, TAAG Angola Airlines, transferred its international operations in October 2025, while the wider transition was completed in March 2026. The airport forms part of Angola's ambition to establish a major Southern African aviation hub. The approximately $3 billion facility is designed to handle 15 million passengers annually, supported by two runways and substantial cargo infrastructure.

TAAG Angola Airlines, TAP, Air France, Lufthansa, Ethiopian, Qatar Airways, Royal Air Maroc, Airlink

However, its initial traffic has been considerably lower than anticipated. Just over 750,000 passengers used the airport during 2025, although that figure reflects a transitional year before all scheduled airlines had relocated. Despite its ambitious scale, the airport faces challenges attracting and retaining international services.

Turkish Airlines removed Luanda from its network in 2026, following the withdrawal of Brussels Airlines last year. Nevertheless, TAP, Lufthansa, Air France, and several African carriers maintain connections. TAP's planned A321LR substitution illustrates how it is able to adjust capacity to demand and still maintain the nonstop service.

#6217. 25 Best Credit Card Offers & Bonuses For Travel Rewards In November 2026

For those with access to credit cards in the United States, the single best way to rack up a lot of points quickly is by taking advantage of the best credit card welcome bonuses and offers. The credit card industry in the United States is lucrative (for banks, airlines, hotel groups, etc.), and the idea is that they often offer large upfront welcome offers and bonuses to incentivize people to apply.

So in this post, I’d like to share what I consider to be the best current credit card welcome bonuses and offers for earning travel rewards, across a variety of categories. The details of the best offers are always changing, so that’s why I think it’s useful to keep a current list with the best credit card welcome bonuses, which I try to constantly update to reflect offers.

I’ll share what I consider the 25 best credit card welcome offers right now to be, across five categories (business transferable points cards, personal transferable points cards, hotel cards, airline cards, and no annual fee cards). Before I do, let me just point out a few things:

Simply put, most people want to travel better, but don’t know how. One of the best ways to improve your travel experience is to pick up an excellent credit card that can add value to your wallet.

When applying for a credit card, consider three main points:

In this post I’m focusing primarily on the best credit card welcome bonuses, which can be one of the best ways to get rewarded quickly. Often a good credit card bonus will be enough to earn you an international ticket in first or business class, which many would otherwise assume is off limits.

Business credit cards tend to have among the most lucrative welcome offers of any cards out there, so if you’re eligible to apply for them, there are some incredible opportunities. Admittedly these cards often have large minimum spending requirements, but if you can unlock them, these cards can earn you an incredible amount of travel.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on business cards that earn travel rewards. Specifically, these are focused on transferable points currencies, which give you the most flexibility (I’ll cover some airline and hotel business cards below, in separate sections).

Personal credit cards are of course the most popular for those looking to earn travel rewards for their credit card spending. These cards can be all over the place in terms of their annual fees and perks, but many are worth having.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on personal cards that earn travel rewards. Specifically, these are focused on transferable points currencies, which give you the most flexibility (I’ll cover some airline and hotel personal cards below, in separate sections).

I’m a huge fan of hotel credit cards, given the incredible value they can offer on an ongoing basis. Even if you don’t spend a lot on these cards, there’s potentially value to having them, thanks to their perks, like hotel elite status, free night awards, and more.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on hotel credit cards, including both personal and business cards.

There’s lots of merit to getting airline credit cards, given that they can offer priority perks and fee waivers for travel on airlines, and can also help you earn elite status.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on airline credit cards, including both personal and business cards.

Admittedly the best credit card welcome offers are typically going to be on credit cards with annual fees. After all, those are typically the most perks-rich cards, and also the ones that card issuers most want to incentivize consumers to apply for. I recognize that some people just absolutely don’t want to pay an annual fee, so it’s worth compiling those offers as well.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on no annual fee credit cards, including both personal and business cards.

Before applying for the best credit card welcome bonuses, makes sure you’re aware of the rules each bank has for credit card applications. One of the common misconceptions people have is that they think applying for credit cards will hurt their credit. The opposite is largely true, actually. Assuming you use your credit responsibly (and make payments on time, don’t utilize too much of your credit, etc.), applying for credit cards can actually help your credit.

However, if you are going to apply for credit cards, make sure you do so responsibly — only apply for them if you have self-control and won’t end up in debt, and try to pay your balance in full every month, or else the interest charges will negate any rewards earned.

Taking advantage of the best credit card welcome bonuses and offers is the fastest way to rack up travel rewards, in order to book first and business class flights, stay at luxury hotels, etc. The best offers are always changing, so it’s worth understanding what the best deals at any given point are.

Of course you’ll also want to consider picking cards that match your long term travel goals, as there’s lots of value to travel credit cards beyond just the welcome offers.

#6216. Marriott Becomes Giant Anti-ICE Billboard As L.A. Protesters Project ‘Blood Money’ Onto Its Walls

Protesters turned a the Warner Center Marriott Woodland Hills into a giant anti-ICE billboard Sunday night, projecting “Marriott takes blood money from ICE” onto its exterior while the hotel’s own logo remained lit up beside it. Spotted at Woodland Hills Marriott where ICE is reportedly staying. — Raider (@iwillnotbesilenced.bsky.social) November 9, 2026 The messages include “Marriott houses the Gestapo,” “Marriott loves Trump” (with a heart), and “Marriott devours your tax dollars for fascism.” The closing message is: “We beat you before. We will beat you again.” Woodland Hills Indivisible had publicized the allegation on November 6, saying its community network had confirmed agents were staying there. A separate event listing advertised an “ICE OUT OF MARRIOTT” demonstration for Sunday evening, and here’s footage of the protest. This was posted on BlueSky, so naturally replies support a Marriott boycott, with one commenter listing out the brands because even Marriott execs can’t name them all. Another offers, “Projector resistance is an underappreciated art form.” And someone asks, “Motel 6 forget to leave the lights on?” I covered Motel 6 properties handing guest lists to ICE, and the chain’s subsequent $7.6 million settlement. Reporting your own guests to immigration authorities is a very different business strategy than renting rooms to the federal government. The Trump Hotel Got This Treatment, Too This immediately brings to mind the projections I wrote about at the former Trump International Hotel in Washington, D.C. in 2017. Artist Robin Bell projected “Emoluments Welcome” and “Pay Trump Bribes Here,” with an arrow pointing toward the entrance. He also displayed the Constitution’s emoluments clause. Projecting Light Isn’t Trespassing So can someone actually do this? In Wilson v. Interlake Steel, California’s Supreme Court said nondamaging intrusions of light, noise, or odor aren’t trespass. However, Light shining into occupied rooms would be nuisance if it’s sufficiently substantial and unreasonable. Actually putting the projection equipment on hotel property or blocking access could be actionable. And LA’s sign ordinance could be implicated – Los Angeles includes projected images in its sign definitions, with restrictions on supergraphic signs. I think it’s an interesting legal queston whether a temporary political display can be restricted based on a municipal sign ordinance but a neutral time, place and manner restriction seems plausible. Renting Rooms To Agents Isn’t The Same As Running A Detention Center The hotel is in HM Alpha Hotels & Resorts’ management portfolio. When HM Alpha announced taking over management, it identified the property as part of Southwest Value Partners’ portfolio. The hotel’s operator makes booking decisions, but a protest aimed at the Marriott name can spread the cost across the brand. Customers generally book a Marriott, not a particular real estate investment firm’s management arrangement. Still, renting an agent a room doesn’t establish that Marriott “loves Trump.” Back in 2019, Marriott, Hilton and Choice said they wouldn’t turn their hotels into immigration detention facilities. Marriott was also criticized for hosting a Customs and Border Protection trade symposium at the Marriott Marquis Chicago. I supported then-CEO Arne Sorenson’s argument that renting meeting space doesn’t mean endorsing a group’s views. Hotels shouldn’t need to agree with their guests’ politics before handing over a room key. I also covered Hilton telling properties to stop housing detained children, followed by government records showing children held at Hilton, Marriott and Choice properties. And Marriott’s neutrality claim looked awfully selective when a Prague hotel rejected a Uyghur conference. In January, Hilton removed a Minnesota Hampton Inn from its system after it continued refusing Homeland Security bookings. I’m not sure that refusing these bookings is something that the property would even be allowed to do, though post-midterms a lot of this is probably up in the air. And indeed the President himself has just walked back his own administration’s tough on immigration stance. (HT: Paul H) Topics on this pageProtestArne M. The hotel’s operator makes booking decisions, but a protest aimed at the Marriott name can spread the cost across the brand. Customers generally book a Marriott, not a particular real estate investment firm’s management arrangement. Still, renting an agent a room doesn’t establish that Marriott “loves Trump.”

Back in 2019, Marriott, Hilton and Choice said they wouldn’t turn their hotels into immigration detention facilities. Marriott was also criticized for hosting a Customs and Border Protection trade symposium at the Marriott Marquis Chicago.

I supported then-CEO Arne Sorenson’s argument that renting meeting space doesn’t mean endorsing a group’s views. Hotels shouldn’t need to agree with their guests’ politics before handing over a room key.

I also covered Hilton telling properties to stop housing detained children, followed by government records showing children held at Hilton, Marriott and Choice properties. And Marriott’s neutrality claim looked awfully selective when a Prague hotel rejected a Uyghur conference.

In January, Hilton removed a Minnesota Hampton Inn from its system after it continued refusing Homeland Security bookings. I’m not sure that refusing these bookings is something that the property would even be allowed to do, though post-midterms a lot of this is probably up in the air. And indeed the President himself has just walked back his own administration’s tough on immigration stance.

The Brand New IHG One Rewards Premier Select Credit Card

As High As 175,000 points. Find Out Your Offer.

If you've ever rented a car, you've probably been asked whether you want to pay extra for insurance at the counter. But depending on which credit card you have, you may already have some coverage.

Many travel rewards credit cards offer rental car insurance that can protect you against theft or damage to your rental vehicle, potentially saving you from paying extra for the rental company's collision damage waiver.

Here's how credit card rental car insurance works, what it covers and which cards offer some of the best protection.

These cards offer primary rental car coverage on eligible rentals. Coverage can vary by card, rental location and purpose.

The information for the United Club Business has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

These cards offer primary car rental insurance, as long as you use your card to pay for the entire rental. Note that this isn’t an exhaustive list; you may find other cards offering primary insurance.

The , and each provide primary car rental insurance for rentals of up to 31 consecutive days. The personal cards are primary, while the business card is primary in the U.S. only for business rentals.

This policy covers theft, damage, valid loss-of-use charges, administrative fees and reasonable towing charges due to covered theft or damage.

Policy details vary slightly among the three cards, though. A key difference is the total amount that can be reimbursed for damages caused by theft or collision:

To learn more about each card, read our full reviews for the Sapphire Preferred, Sapphire Reserve and Sapphire Reserve for Business.

The Capital One Venture X and Venture X Business both offer primary rental car insurance, though the coverage terms differ.

The personal Venture X provides reimbursement for theft and collision damage up to the actual cash value of eligible rental vehicles with an original manufacturer's suggested retail price of $75,000 or less. Coverage applies to rentals of up to 15 consecutive days in your country of residence or 31 consecutive days elsewhere.

Meanwhile, the Venture X Business provides primary coverage for eligible rentals made primarily for business purposes, covering theft and collision damage subject to the policy's valuation limits. Rentals of up to 31 consecutive days are eligible for coverage.

To learn more, read our full reviews of the Venture X and Venture X Business.

Learn more: Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card

Learn more: Capital One Venture X Business

Four of the Ink Business cards from Chase offer primary insurance when you rent for business purposes, providing reimbursement for theft and collision damage for most rental vehicles with an MSRP of $125,000 or less.

Each card provides reimbursement of up to $60,000 for theft and collision damage.

To learn more, read our guide to the Chase Ink Business cards.

United’s cobranded cards offer primary car rental insurance, though the business versions are primary only when you rent for business purposes. You need to decline the rental company’s collision insurance and charge the entire rental cost to your card.

This insurance provides reimbursement of up to $60,000 for theft and collision damage for most rental vehicles with an MSRP of $125,000 or less.

To learn more, read our guide to the United cards.

Among the most important factors here is making sure you pay for your entire car rental bill with a credit card that has an auto collision damage waiver included in its benefits. You'll also want to decline any insurance offer from your rental car company.

Of course, terms and conditions vary, so always check your card's specific policies before you rent. This way, if you run into a problem, you'll know what's covered and what's not.

If you don’t follow these requirements, your credit card car rental insurance won’t take effect.

Related: All you need to know about using a debit card to rent a car

The car rental insurance from your credit card is technically called an “auto rental collision damage waiver.” This benefit provides reimbursement for damage due to collision or theft. The cash amount your card's insurance policy will cover can vary, so check your card's guide to benefits for specific details.

While some cards also cover loss-of-use and towing charges assessed by the rental company, policies from other credit cards only cover physical damage or theft of the rental vehicle. Knowing what your card will cover is important before you use it.

Additionally, some rental types and locations may not be eligible for coverage. Keep the following provisions in mind if you rely on credit card car rental insurance benefits:

If you have doubts about your car's eligibility, it's best practice to call the customer service number on your card. You can get more information and confirm that your policy covers your rental vehicle type in the country you’ll be visiting.

Related: My experience with Turo: Car rental convenience at a great price

Another important distinction is the difference between primary and secondary car rental insurance, as your card could offer one type or the other. Both types of insurance usually have maximum coverage amounts, so make sure these meet or exceed the total value of the car you’re renting.

If you get into an accident with your rental car and have primary insurance, you only need to file one claim. Generally, primary insurance will reimburse you for the rental car’s cash value or the cost to repair it, whichever is less.

Secondary insurance is different because it only reimburses you for the amount not covered by other types of insurance, such as travel insurance or personal car insurance. However, if you don’t own a car or carry a car insurance policy, most secondary insurance from credit cards will become primary.

Select American Express cards include secondary coverage for damage to or theft of an eligible rental car. If you want primary coverage, you can enroll an eligible Amex card in Premium Car Rental Protection before you rent. Amex charges a flat fee per eligible rental paid for with the enrolled card.

Related: Secondary rental car insurance: Best cards and what's covered

Many consumers focus on the number of points or miles they can earn and redeem when choosing a travel rewards card, but travel protections such as rental car insurance can also provide significant value.

However, reviewing your card’s policy details is essential to understand what is (and isn’t) covered. Don’t assume you’re covered for every possible mishap when you pay for a car rental with a credit card that offers insurance, as many exceptions and exclusions apply.

Ensure you know the details and how they relate to your rental location, vehicle type, length of rental period and other important issues so you won’t be surprised by a bill if your rental car has a problem.

#6214. Washington Dulles Concourse E Opens, With Huge New United Club

United Airlines is on quite the roll when it comes to opening new concourses and lounges at its hubs. Just recently, I covered how a new United Club opened in Houston (IAH) Terminal B North. This is not only the biggest United Club in the world, but it’s the biggest airport lounge in all of the Americas.

There’s now another update, as we’re seeing the opening of a new United Club at Washington Dulles (IAD) Concourse E. This is the second biggest United Club in the entire system, and it’s also part of a long overdue new concourse for the airport. Let’s first talk about the new lounge, and then about the new concourse.

A brand new United Club is opening in Concourse E at Washington Dulles Airport. The new lounge is nearly 40,000 square feet, with seating for more than 600 customers, making it the carrier’s second largest United Club in the system. Crucially, this also increases United’s club and lounge space at the airport by nearly 70%.

The new lounge has a bar, two buffet stations, eight private phone rooms, complimentary Wi-Fi, and power access at nearly every seat. Unfortunately there are no showers or barista coffee.

As the design is described, it “reflects the character of the Washington, D.C. region through design elements inspired by the historic natural and built environment of the nation’s capital, like the iconic main Dulles terminal architecture, cherry blossoms and the Blue Ridge Mountains.”

The club is located across from gates E14 and E16, and it’s open daily from 5:30AM until 10PM, with an opening on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The lounge follows the standard United Club access policies.

The opening of the new United Club is part of the larger opening of the new Concourse E at Washington Dulles. This is the first new concourse to open at the airport in two decades.

The new concourse is 435,000 square feet, and it has 14 new gates that will exclusively be used by United. United claims that these new gates will increase connectivity by nearly 30% during peak times. The concourse also has direct AeroTrain access, expansive new dining and retail options, and more.

It’s important to keep in mind what a mess United’s current facility at Washington Dulles is, which is what makes this all the more exciting. United primarily operates out of Concourses C and D, which were built as temporary facilities in 1985. 40+ years later, they’re still there. So this new concourse will be a massive boost to the United passenger experience.

We know that Dulles Airport is supposed to undergo a major modernization, which was unveiled by the Trump administration. However, the cost is astronomical (even by the typically inflated airport standards), and things are already well behind schedule.

As you’d expect, this press release has endless quotes from airline, airport, and Trump administration officials. There’s also a fair bit of spin here, like this, from Deputy Secretary of Transportation, Steven Bradbury:

“Under President Trump, America is building again. So far, the construction of United’s new Concourse E has supported 2,700 good paying jobs and brought $1.3 billion in local economic activity to the national capital region. USDOT’s broader partnership with MWAA and United on the Dulles Airport transformation is just beginning, with many more milestones on the horizon. The ultimate winner will be the American people who will enjoy a stunning new gateway to America’s capital for generations to come. Congratulations to MWAA and United for today’s grand unveiling, and we look forward to even greater results in the near future.”

Keep in mind that the “building” of this concourse started under the Biden administration, and not under the Trump administration.

Washington Dulles Airport’s new Concourse E opens to the public on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The new concourse adds 14 gates for United, and most importantly, it looks like a real terminal, and not like a temporary facility. The concourse has a new United Club, which not only looks much improved, but also massively increases lounge capacity.

What do you make of Washington Dulles Airport’s new Concourse, and the new United Club?

#6213. How To Max Out Citi Strata Elite’s Impressive Credits

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

I’ve been looking forward not just to spending a big initial bonus – now 75,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 in the first 3 months of account opening – but to making the most out of all of the credits that come with the Citi Strata EliteSM Card (See rates and fees.) As a new cardholder I dove into the specifics of the benefits. So here’s what to expect.

The Citi Strata EliteSM Card offers an annual $200 Splurge Credit. You receive up to $200 back on retailers including 1stDibs, American Airlines, Best Buy, Future Personal Training, and Live Nation. This benefit is on a calendar year basis. So during your first cardmember year you can actually claim it twice – once during the remainder of 2026, and again at the start of 2027. You can redeem it across one or more transactions. You don’t need to try to max it out in a single transaction – you won’t simply lose the remainder. In order to use the credit you first need to register for it and select up to two merchants at a time you’d like to use the credit for. The selection applies immediately (in fact, as of 12 a.m. Eastern time on the day you made the selection.) It may take up to to billing cycles to receive the credit. The credits can be used at two of 1stDibs; Live Nation; Best Buy; American Airlines; Future Personal Training. Bear in mind that some transactions won’t qualify – it’s based on the merchant of record: American Airlines or American Airlines Vacations needs to bill for the splurge credit to count. If you book related products and services with a different merchant of record (which even includes AAdvantage status renewal) those won’t count. Live Nation purchases need to be made at livenation.com or ticketmaster.com- – and for events held in the United States – third party fulfilled purchases won’t trigger the credit. The credit is super easy to use. I’ll just use the card for an American Airlines ticket. (This needs to be booked directly, not through Citi Travel or another travel portal.) Don’t have a booking right away and you’re about to hit end of year? Avoid basic economy fares, but buy a non-refundable ticket. If you cancel the ticket you’ll retain an American Airlines trip credit for future use. Or select Best Buy and make a purchase there. $100 Semi-Annual Blacklane Credit Blacklane sets up car services for you all over the world. It’s mostly pre-reserved. They’re in a lot more places than Uber and you’re getting a professional driver. At airports you’ll usually have them meet you at baggage claim and assist with luggage, for instance. And you’re going to get more consistently nice vehicles and better service than rideshare. They track your flight, arrive in advance and wait for you for an allowable time (like an hour). The card offers a $200 credit each year with Blacklane – $100 January – June and $100 July – December. No registration is required, just pay for Blacklane trips with the card and the statement credits trigger automatically. In London, Paris and Dubai I use Wheely. Most of the time in the U.S. I’ll use rideshare. But with my family, arriving after a couple of weeks abroad, I may want a car service pickup because the Austin airport makes you schlepp across the road and through a parking structure, changing levels, to reach rideshare pickup. Pre-arranged cars park by the terminal, and the driver is there to help with luggage. Pricing varies by airport and trip, but it’s often competitive with premium Uber services like BlackSUV. $300 Hotel Benefit Each year, Citi Strata Elite Card offers a $300 hotel credit for stays of two or more nights that are prepaid through Citi Travel. (Prepaid rates can still be cancellable and refundable.) The credit must be redeemed by the primary cardmember and is by calendar year (based on when you book, not the dates of your stay). A new cardmember could use the credit now and again at the start of 2027, so twice in their first cardmember year. $300 will be applied to your booking when you make the reservation – it’s not a statement credit that posts later. You can also use it across multiple transactions, e.g. if you had a 2-night stay that totaled only $200 you’d still have $100 to use later. While the card earns 12x on hotels you use it to pay for with Citi Travel, you don’t earn points on the charges covered by this credit. Consider these OTA bookings. Pricing can vary and you’re often getting the same rate as elsewhere – but not discounted rates like AAA, or member rates. You also aren’t usually entitled to hotel loyalty points, elite stay credit, or elite benefits. Priority Pass The card offers a Priority Pass Select membership for the primary cardmember and any authorized users (which are $75 each), valid for unlimited visits and including up to two complimentary guests.. It does not cover credits at restaurants and similar non-lounge offerings like markets that are linked to Priority Pass. You don’t need to have your physical or even digital Priority Pass membership for access – rather uniquely lounges are supposed to accept your Strata Elite card as the Priority Pass card itself. That means, unlike other issuers, you don’t have to activate Priority Pass membership. Marco Polo Lounge, Venice Admirals Club Passes The card comes with 4 Admirals Club passes per calendar year (so twice in cardmember year one, for eight passes total). Each set of four has to be used during the calendar year in which they’re issued, and expire if unused. They are available to the primary cardmember and include one guest 18 years or older plus up to 3 children under 18. They can be redeemed for additional adult companions as well. Requires same day boarding pass (departing or arriving) for an American or oneworld partner airline flight. Valid for 24 hours, and can be used at multiple lounges on the same day. The passes are deposited to your AAdvanage wallet and can be scanned by the Admirals Club front desk for entry. Upon card account closure, unused passes are forfeit. Admirals Club Washington National Airport E Concourse Applying For This Card Was An Easy Decision Citi’s new premium card is pretty incredible in the first year, not just because of the strong initial bonus but also because of credits that are timed to calendar year rather than cardmember year. (Calendar year credits can be claimed twice in cardmember year one.) Honestly, I feel like this was a strategic error on Citi’s part. They’ve constructed a card that is a no-brainer to get. There’s just so much value to the customer up front. I’m not sure if it’ll be a keeper long-term or a card that’s best for your everyday spend (although it is very good). My take: apply for this card, reap the maximum benefits in year one, and then consider whether it’s right for you in the long-term.
